Metadata.CommitMsg:
threat model: the scheduled audit is a fourth mode, not a variant of the third

The document named three ways this is used and missed one that already ships.
templates/audit-cronjob.yaml runs the audit on a timer inside Kubernetes, and
it is not the churn rig with a schedule attached. It differs in the thing that
matters: it runs forever without anyone deciding to run it.

Modes 1 and 3 are started by a person. Mode 2 runs when a pipeline is
triggered. This one is a standing unattended process holding a live
credential, so its risk is duration rather than privilege. The same credential,
exposed continuously instead of for one job. Compromise gives recurring access
that killing the pod does not end, plus the manifest on its volume, which is a
map of the repository. Disclosure, not destruction.

Nobody reviews it and nobody needs to, for one reason worth stating rather
than assuming: the scheduled process cannot delete. reclaim/ is never imported
on the audit path, so there is no --execute to reach. Review stands between a
wrong answer and an irreversible act, and there is no irreversible act here. A
wrong manifest is a wrong report.

The temptation this creates is the dangerous part, and it is why the mode
earns its own section rather than a sentence. A scheduled audit produces a
manifest nobody reads, and the obvious next step is to have something act on
it. That step removes the property that makes scheduling safe. It is issue 13
now, with the options and the thing that must not happen written down, rather
than a configuration change someone makes on a Friday.
